1.explanation:
• src/overlay/utils/position.js  
  This module computes and applies the absolute (or fixed) top/left for every Overlay. The bug with two nested scroll containers means the parent-offset or scroll offsets aren’t being factored in correctly. This is the heart of the mis-position issue.  

• src/overlay/popup.jsx  
  Popup controls how we choose the container (via the container callback and followTrigger) and how we wrap the trigger/content. A tweak here may be needed to ensure we use the right offsetParent or wrapperStyle when there are multiple scrollbars.  

• src/number-picker/number-picker.jsx  
  The NumberPicker component declares innerBefore but doesn’t handle innerAfter in render() or in its layout calculations, so any suffix breaks alignment or disappears. This file needs to be updated to support an innerAfter prop and to integrate its width/margin into the input’s wrapper.  

• src/number-picker/style.js  
  This file pulls in the SCSS/CSS for NumberPicker. To get innerBefore/innerAfter to align correctly, you’ll likely need to add or adjust selectors here (or in the imported main.scss) for the extra wrapper elements so they flow around the input as intended.
1.bug_scenario:
1. Overlay position: In a scrollable container nested inside another scrollable area (two scrollbars), when you open the DatePicker’s popup, scroll down a little and then reopen it, the overlay is rendered at the wrong coordinates—out of sync with the trigger’s actual position.  
2. NumberPicker innerBefore/innerAfter: You can pass an innerBefore node and it shows (albeit a little off), but innerAfter is not supported—either it doesn’t render at all or it breaks the input layout. The first screenshot shows a standalone NumberPicker with “before” and “after” labels misaligned around the input; the second shows the same problem in a real form, where the port-spinner controls and the custom suffix are not lining up correctly.
